question: Where a unit's counter covers a building picture - an air unit at its base under a land stack - which does a click on the map pick?
slots_noted: CCounterObject::HitTest is CCounterObject slot 20 and CHoiAvatar::HitTest CHoiAvatar slot 20, both already in the record under those names; this fragment only revises their comments and confidence.

addresses.name: CBillboardObject::HitTest
addresses.revises: confidence inferred to confirmed, the 1.0 and -1.0 read off the bytes; the comment adds what the score means to ProvinceGraphics_HitTest
addresses.signature: float __thiscall CBillboardObject::HitTest(CBillboardObject* this, float x, float y, float* matrix, float a, float b, float c, int d, int e)
addresses.comment: Slot 20: whether a point of the screen is on the billboard. Asks its type's slot 32 (0xB07A50, not read) with (&x, &the world transform +0x94, its frame (slot 25), its draw scale +0xB28) and answers **1.0 on a hit** (`fld1`) and **-1.0 on a miss** (the float at 0x170AC0C). `ret 0x20`. The score a building picture and a large base picture bring to ProvinceGraphics_HitTest, where a counter's is at least 1.1, so a counter over one always wins the click. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-billboardfx.md, section 2, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0xAB6ED0..0xAB6F21: the hit exit is `fld1; pop ebp; ret 0x20`, the miss `fld dword [0x170AC0C]`, read off the image as -1.0. Wrong if slot 20 of the building pictures is not this body (vtable.py holding 0xAB6ED0 would show it elsewhere).

addresses.name: CCounterObject::HitTest
addresses.revises: confidence inferred to confirmed - the score had been read in the decompiled C only - with its constants and field named; the comment adds that any counter beats a building picture
addresses.signature: float __thiscall CCounterObject::HitTest(CCounterObject* this, float x, float y, float* matrix, float a, float b, float c, int d, int e)
addresses.comment: **Slot 20: whether a point of the screen is on the counter.** Asks CCounterType_IsPointOnQuad (0x83C2B0) with the counter's scale and answers **`(order + 1) * 0.1 + 1`** on a hit - `+0x1A8` the order, the doubles at 0x160A3C0 (0.1) and 0x160A248 (1.0) - and **-1.0** on a miss (the float at 0x170AC0C), so that of several the one highest in its stack wins, and any counter beats a building picture's 1.0 in ProvinceGraphics_HitTest. `ret 0x20`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x839620..0x8396AE: the hit exit is `fild (+0x1A8 + 1); fmul [0x160A3C0]; fadd [0x160A248]`, the miss `fld [0x170AC0C]`; the three constants read off the image as 0.1, 1.0 and -1.0. Wrong if +0x1A8 can be below nought, which would let a counter score under 1.0 (how +0x1A8 is set was not read).

addresses.name: CHoiAvatar::HitTest
addresses.revises: comment only: the far branch read off the bytes, answering the counter's own score
addresses.signature: float __thiscall CHoiAvatar::HitTest(CHoiAvatar* this, float x, float y, float* matrix, float a, float b, float c, int d, int e)
addresses.comment: Slot 20. With `seen_from_far` (+0x152) it asks `unit_counter` (+0x13C) where that is shown and **answers the counter's own score**, the call through the counter's slot 20 being its last before the epilogue; else with the setting at CSettings +0xF9 it asks `unit_counter_close` (+0x140) where that is the top counter of one of its province's stacks; else it tests the figure. So the near view is counters or figures by a setting, and the far view counters always. The far branch read off the bytes; the near ones likely. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x84A2F0..0x84A384: with +0x152 set and +0x13C shown (its slot 15), the counter's slot 20 is called with the arguments passed on and the function returns with st(0) untouched. The near branches (from 0x84A387) were not read past their tests. Wrong if a near counter's answer is scaled before it is returned.

addresses.name: ProvinceGraphics_HitTest
addresses.revises: comment only: the score comparison and its strictness, what each kind of picture scores, and that building pictures are skipped while one unit is selected
addresses.signature: void* __stdcall ProvinceGraphics_HitTest(void* owner, void* provinceGraphics, float* mouse, CList* selection)
addresses.comment: **What a click on a province's pictures picks** (MapGraphics_PickUnderPointer asks it after the battles). Each picture is asked by its 3D object's slot 20 for a ray from the mouse through the camera's projection, and **kept only where its score is strictly above the best so far** (`jbe` at 0x64109F against nought, 0x64111B, 0x6412FA), the best starting at nought: a building or large base picture scores 1.0 (CBillboardObject::HitTest), a counter `(order + 1) * 0.1 + 1` (CCounterObject::HitTest), so **a counter over a building picture always wins**. The large air base picture (+0x7C) offers the air base's selectable (CMapProvince +0x54, +0x18; kind 8), the large naval base picture (+0x80) the CPort (+0x354; kind 4). **sel**: where exactly one thing is selected, of kind 0, 1 or 2, and its own avatar (+0x164) is under the mouse. With the camera at 500 or under, each 3D object of the province (+0x10, +0xDC, next +0xD8) scoring above the best so far: where the counters are on (settings word bit 0x800), the province's unit vector (+0x2C8) at its cursor (+0x2E8) is asked - with the camera above counter_distance and that unit not selected and not at its own base, it alone (intel 2 or more) is taken where this object is its avatar; otherwise the vector is walked round from the cursor, and **with sel every unit in sel's province, of sel's owner and not at its own base is gathered in that order** and the walk stops; without sel the unit whose avatar this object is wins. Then, **only without sel** (0x641479), where the buildings are on (bit 0x20), the object shown and the province not hidden by fog, a building picture (+0x40 vector) offers the CPort for a naval base, the air base's selectable for an air base, the building (kind 6) otherwise. **With sel the answer is the unit after sel in what was gathered, wrapping** - so clicking the one selected unit's counter again picks the next of its owner's units in the province; sel alone answers itself. Otherwise the best hit, or 0. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: The score comparisons (0x641093..0x64109F, 0x64110E..0x64111B, 0x6412ED..0x6412FA) and the building branch's entry test at 0x641479 (`cmp [ebp-0x18], 0; jne 0x641566`, [ebp-0x18] being sel as stored at 0x641176) disassembled 2026-11-13; the two slot 20 bodies' answers confirmed off the bytes. The rest is the selection reading's, unchanged. Wrong if a counter can score under 1.0 (CCounterObject +0x1A8 below nought).

frontier: 0xB07A50 - a billboard type's slot 32, the point-on-quad test CBillboardObject::HitTest asks; only its boolean answer matters to the click
how CCounterObject +0x1A8 (a counter's order in its stack) is set
whether land counters are drawn in the air map mode, which decides whether the large air base picture there is ever under one
